dhp221:1:
Abandon anger,
be done with conceit,
dhp221:3:
When for name & form
you have no attachment
–have nothing at all–
no sufferings, no stresses, invade.
dhp222:2:
whoever keeps firm control
as if with a racing chariot:
dhp222:3:
him
I call a master charioteer.
dhp222:4:
Anyone else,
a rein-holder–
that’s all.
dhp223:1:
Conquer anger
with lack of anger;
dhp224:1:
By telling the truth;
by not growing angry;
dhp224:2:
by giving, when asked,
no matter how little you have:
dhp224:4: you enter the presence of devas.
dhp225:4:
where, having gone,
there’s no grief.
dhp226:4: their effluents come to an end.
dhp227:1: This has come down from old, Atula,
dhp227:3:
they find fault with one
who sits silent,
dhp227:4:
they find fault with one
who speaks a great deal,
dhp227:5:
they find fault with one
who measures his words.
dhp227:6: There’s no one unfaulted in the world.
dhp228:3:
anyone entirely faulted
or entirely praised.
If knowledgeable people praise him,
dhp229:3: to be blameless in conduct, intelligent,
dhp230:2: who’s fit to find fault with him?
dhp231:1:
Guard against anger
erupting in body;
dhp231:4:
live conducting yourself well
in body.
dhp232:1:
Guard against anger
erupting in speech;
dhp232:4:
live conducting yourself well
in speech.
dhp233:1:
Guard against anger
erupting in mind;
dhp233:4:
live conducting yourself well
in mind.
dhp234:4:
–enlightened–
are the ones whose restraint is secure.
